source: E. B. Cowell and J. Eggeling, Catalogue of Buddhist Sanskrit Manuscripts in the possession of the Royal Asiatic Society (Hodgson Collection), JRAS 8.1 (1875), parsed from uploaded OCR/VL scan

source_control.catalogue_baseline: The catalogue states that manuscript material is Indian paper unless otherwise stated.
source_control.support_correction: Direct entry review finds 12 explicit palm-leaf manuscripts, not 10 as recorded in ras_hodgson_material_catalogue_census_v0_1/v0_2. Entries 34 and 37 were omitted by the earlier keyword census.
source_control.dimension_coverage: 78 of 79 entries have usable dimensions after explicit field inheritance for MSS 78-79 and cautious cross-witness recovery for MS 17; MS 53 remains unresolved because OCR corrupts the fractional long dimension.
source_control.warning: This is a cross-sectional catalogue census, not a matched before/after copy series. Support-format association does not by itself prove that an individual text changed geometry when copied from palm leaf to paper.

descriptive_result: Palm-leaf and paper manuscripts occupy overlapping long-dimension scales: median long dimension is 12.25 in. for palm leaf and 11.5 in. for paper.
The short dimension separates much more strongly: median 2.0 in. for palm leaf versus 3.0 in. for paper.
Aspect ratio therefore shifts from a median 6.696 for palm leaf to 3.640 for paper.
11 of 12 palm-leaf manuscripts have aspect ratio >=5, compared with 8 of 66 dimensioned paper manuscripts.
10 of 12 palm-leaf manuscripts have short dimension <=2.25 in., compared with 6 of 66 dimensioned paper manuscripts.
The safest paper-history formulation is long-axis overlap with short-axis expansion, not simple preservation of palm-leaf geometry.
interpretive_limits: Do not describe the corpus statistics as direct evidence of a chronological material transition.
Do not infer that paper caused width expansion without matched copy histories.
Do not treat all paper manuscripts as Western codex forms; many remain horizontally oblong.
Direct object inspection is required for sheet structure, trimming, ruling, watermark, chain lines and binding.

dimension_exceptions.status: dimensions inherited by explicit catalogue cross-reference from MS 77
